title: Headless published-content delivery for application consumers
description:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As an application developer, I want a minimal versioned JSON delivery contract for published Papyrus content, so that applications can consume articles without depending on a page renderer or internal CMS schema.

Definition of Done for later implementation: documented v1 contract, individual article retrieval, list/filter/pagination and public asset references, common visibility/update handling and isolation specifications. Structured fields plus a Markus body string are required; renderer-specific HTML or body IR is not a required interchange contract. Depends on the shared foundation; examine existing Published* and Markus/S3 projection before choosing static JSON versus request-time transport. Reuse M8 PPY-f293ea where appropriate; its latest/search JSON lacks the full article contract. No new publishing engine.

Deferred/YAGNI: Markdown+YAML export, exact Contentful API compatibility, extra export formats and authenticated draft previews. This is delivery for public application consumers, not an editorial API or a new authoring backend.

Approved post-save platform behavior: when headless delivery is enabled, publish, saved published edits and unpublish automatically refresh its outputs consistently with article/listings/indexes, sitemap and RSS/Atom. Private draft saves never enter public delivery. Ancillary failures must be visible/retryable. Detailed observable acceptance is in PPY-defff04e-17b5-4e28-9bb5-df412601a102. Implementation remains unstarted.

Organizing initiative: Markus for everything (PPY-23a743). This is one architecture with shared authored pages, includes/derived regeneration, published projection and delivery contracts. RSS/Atom and headless remain dependent on the shared foundation and post-save behavior. Incremental vertical slices are allowed as future planning, but a bespoke custom-Python composition shortcut contradicts the target design. Monitoring remains separate and linked, not a prerequisite. This architecture is now lower priority than the real Monitoring learning-loop slice; no implementation is authorized for it.

## Public page alternate extension — planning only, 2026-10-20

Extend the existing headless work with a discoverable Markus/Markdown
representation of **each public published page**, including the homepage,
ordinary product/help/wiki pages and published editorial pages. This extends
the public content and structural context available to authoring agents to
visiting agents; it never extends their access to private authoring context.
The minimal versioned JSON application contract remains in scope.

This is a narrow exception to the earlier deferred Markdown-export wording:
a per-page published reading representation is now planned. Full
Markdown+YAML source/archive export, arbitrary internal metadata and
authenticated draft previews remain deferred. Attach the narrow acceptance
story under this epic; do not create another delivery epic.

Serve a public, human-accessible alternate with HTML `rel="alternate"` and
matching HTTP `Link` discovery and a correct media type. Standard links are
the baseline; optional `Accept` negotiation requires correct weights,
exclusions and cache separation. `llms.txt` is a nonstandard proposal and
optional future index, not required discovery, access control or a promise
that bots follow instructions. The output is content, not hidden prompt
injection or privileged instructions.

Derive both representations from the same public published snapshot using an
explicit allowlist. Preserve public meaning, reading order, headings, links,
citations, media alternatives and meaningful Markus layout relationships.
Exclude drafts, rejected material, version history, private policies/prompts,
internal provenance and hidden metadata; do not publish `frontMatterYaml`,
`bodyIr` or the existing build export wholesale. Supported includes/listings
must expose only their public resolved content and share foundation dependency
refresh, not source query/configuration details. A page is not feed-eligible
merely because it has an alternate.

README rationale: reduce tokens and token cost where the measured representation
is smaller; reduce irrelevant navigation/DOM/script markup in model context so
more context and attention can be spent on the reader's task. Better accuracy
is an intended, testable hypothesis, never a guarantee. Measure token counts
with a named tokenizer, actual tool-visible payloads, semantic fidelity and
task outcomes; compare raw HTML and realistic extracted-content baselines.

Implementation remains unstarted. Reuse the shared foundation
PPY-3f55c3e1-65f6-4fc7-833e-6cecc6a85270 and post-save behavior
PPY-defff04e-17b5-4e28-9bb5-df412601a102; link RSS/Atom
PPY-33854a5d-da97-4597-9ad2-948a7dd23136 and guide
PPY-92de976d-7d0c-40ce-9a3b-2d7de0b6eb7d. This does not change priority or
authorize a runtime deployment.

No code/tests/dependencies/infrastructure/deployment changes; behavior implementation and executable acceptance remain unstarted.
